But it is not for this that God is angry with you, but so that you may turn back your household[a], which has sinned against the Lord and against us[h], their parents. Yet, being fond of your children, you did not admonish your household, but you let it be grievously ruined; for this the Lord is angry with you. But he will heal all the past evils in your household; for because of their sins and lawless deeds you yourself were ruined by worldly affairs.

But the Lord’s abundant compassion has had mercy on you and your household, and he will strengthen you and set you on a foundation in his glory. Only do not be slothful, but take heart and strengthen your household. For, as the blacksmith hammering his work masters the thing he intends, so also the righteous word day by day[e] prevails over every wickedness. Do not, therefore, cease admonishing your children; for I know that if they repent[i][f] with their whole heart, they will be written in the books of life[b] with the holy ones[g].

After these words of hers ceased, she says to me, “Do you wish to hear me reading?” And I say, “I do, Lady.” She says to me, “Become a hearer, and hear the glories of God.” I heard great and wondrous things which I was not able to remember; for all the words were terrifying—things a human being is not able to bear. So I remembered the last words, for they were beneficial and gentle for us:

“Behold, the God of hosts[c], who by his invisible and mighty power and by his great understanding created the world, and by his glorious counsel adorned his creation with beauty, and by his mighty word fixed the heaven and founded the earth upon the waters[d], and by his own wisdom and providence created his holy church, which also he blessed—behold, he is moving the heavens and the mountains and the hills and the seas, and all things become level for his elect, in order that he may give to them the promise which he promised with much glory and joy, if they keep the statutes of God which they received with great faith.”

records.after_text:
After fifteen days[1], when I had been fasting and had asked the Lord many things, the understanding of the writing was revealed to me.[1] And this was written:

“Your offspring, Hermas,[2] have rejected God and blasphemed the Lord, and they have betrayed their parents in great wickedness, and they were heard as betrayers of parents; and though they betrayed them, they gained no advantage, but they added still to their sins licentious acts and interminglings of wickedness,[3] and thus their lawless deeds were filled up.

But make these words known to all your children and to your wife, who is to be your sister;[4] for she too does not refrain from her tongue, by which she acts wickedly. But when she hears these words, she will refrain, and she will obtain mercy.

After you have made known to them these words which the Master commanded me to be revealed to you, then all their sins that they formerly committed are forgiven them, and also to all the holy ones who have sinned up to this day, if they repent[c] with all their heart and remove from their heart their double‑mindedness.[6]

For the Master swore by his glory concerning his chosen ones: if, after this appointed day[2], sin should still occur, they have no salvation; for repentance has an end for the righteous. The days of repentance have been fulfilled for all the holy ones, but for the nations there is repentance until the last day.[9]

Therefore you shall say to those who lead the church[10] that they should set their ways straight in righteousness, so that they may receive the promises in full, with much glory.

Hold fast, then, you who work righteousness, and do not be double‑minded, so that your passage may be with the holy angels.[11] Blessed are you who endure the great tribulation that is coming, and who will not deny their life.[12]

For the Lord swore by his Son[13] that those who denied their Lord are rejected from their life—those who are now about to deny him in the coming days; but to those who denied before, because of his great compassion[b][a][14][13][12][11][10][9][6][4][3], he became merciful.”[14]

After showing me these things[1], she wanted to run off. I say to her, "Lady, what profit is it to me to have seen these things and not know what the matters are?" Answering me, she says, "You are a crafty man, wanting to know the things concerning the tower." "Yes, lady," I say, "so that I may report them to the brothers, and that, becoming more cheerful and hearing these things, they may know the Lord in much glory."

She said, "Many indeed will hear; and, having heard, some of them will rejoice, but some will weep. But even these, if they hear and repent[b], they too will rejoice. Therefore listen to the parables of the tower, for I will reveal everything to you. And no longer cause me trouble about revelations, for these revelations have an end, for they have been completed. But you will not stop asking for revelations, for you are shameless."

"The tower that you see being built is I, the Church, the one shown to you both now and before. Whatever[2], therefore, you wish to inquire about the tower, I will reveal to you, so that you may rejoice with the holy ones."

I say to her, "Lady, since once for all you considered me worthy for everything to be revealed to me, reveal it." She says to me, "Whatever can be revealed to you will be revealed. Only let your heart be toward God, and do not be double-minded in whatever you see."

I asked her, "Why has the tower been built upon the waters, lady?" She says, "I told you before also, and you inquire diligently; therefore, by inquiring, you find the truth. Why, then, the tower has been built upon the waters—listen: because your life was saved through water and will be saved. And the tower has been founded by the word of the Almighty and glorious Name[a][9][8][7][6][5][4][3], and is held fast by the unseen power of the Master."

“Listen now about the stones that go into the building. The stones, then, that are square and white and that fit together at their joints [a]—these are the apostles and bishops [b] and teachers and deacons [c], who walked in the reverent dignity of God [d] and who oversaw and taught and served God’s elect with purity and reverence [e]—some have fallen asleep [f], and some are still alive. They were always in agreement with one another, had peace among themselves, and listened to each other; for this reason their joints fit in the building of the tower.

“And the ones drawn up from the deep [g] and set into the building and fitting together at their joints with the other stones already built—who are they?” “These are the ones who suffered on account of the name of the Lord [h].”

“I want to know who the other stones are that are being carried from the dry land [i], lady.” She said, “Those that go into the building without being hewn [j]—the Lord approved these, because they walked in the uprightness of the Lord [k] and accomplished his commandments [l].”

“And the ones being brought and set into the building—who are they?” “They are new in the faith and faithful [m]. But they are being admonished [n] by the angels to do good, because evil was found in them.”

“And those whom they were casting away and throwing aside [o]—who are they?” “These are people who have sinned and want to repent[t] [p]. But if the building is completed, they no longer have a place, but will be cast out [r]. But they have only this: to lie beside the tower [s].”

As for the other stones that you saw thrown far from the tower and falling into the road and rolling from the road into the pathless places[h]: these are those who have believed[a], but because of their double‑mindedness they abandon their true road. Thinking, then, that they are able to find a better road, they go astray and suffer misery as they walk in the pathless places.

But those that fall into the fire and are burned—these are the ones who have finally turned away from the living God, and it no longer came up into their heart to repent[k][a] because of the cravings of their lewdness[b] and the evils they have done.

And those others that fall near the waters yet are not able to roll into the water—do you want to know who they are? These are the ones who have heard the word and want to be baptized into the name[j] of the Lord; then, when the purity of the truth comes to their remembrance, they change their mind[d] and go back again after their evil desires.

So she finished the explanation of the tower. But, plucking up my courage again, I questioned her further whether all these stones that were cast away and did not fit into the building of the tower—whether there is repentance for them and whether they have a place in this tower. “They have repentance,” she says, “but they cannot fit into this tower.

Rather, they will fit in another place, much smaller[e]; and this will be when they have been tormented and have completed the days of their sins[i]. And for this reason they will be transferred, because they have shared in the righteous word[f]. And then it will happen that they are transferred from their torments, if the evil deeds they have done come up into their heart[g]. But if they do not come up into their heart[f][d][c], they are not saved because of their hardness of heart.”

The vision that I saw[a], brothers, came twenty days after the former vision; it was as a pattern of the tribulation that is coming.

I was going into the countryside by the Campanian road. It is about ten stadia from the public road, and the place is easy to travel.

So, walking alone, I was beseeching the Lord to bring to completion the revelations and the visions that he had shown me through his holy Church, so that he would strengthen me and give repentance[m] to his servants who have stumbled, in order that his great and glorious name might be glorified, because he counted me worthy to show me his wonders.

And while I was glorifying and giving thanks to him, something like the sound of a voice answered me: “Do not be double-minded, Hermas.” I began to reason within myself and say, “What do I have to be double-minded about, being so firmly established by the Lord and having seen glorious things?”

I went on a little, brothers, and behold, I see dust rising as if to the sky, and I began to say within myself, “Perhaps cattle are coming and stirring up dust?” For it was about a stadion away from me[b].

As the dust grew greater and greater, I supposed it was something divine. The sun shone out a little, and behold, I see a very great beast, like some sea monster, and from its mouth fiery locusts were coming out. The beast was about a hundred feet in length, and its head was like a jar.

I began to weep and to ask the Lord that he would deliver me from it. And I remembered the word that I had heard: “Do not be double-minded, Hermas.”

So then, brothers, having put on the faith of the Lord and having remembered the mighty deeds that he had taught me, I took courage and gave myself over to the beast. Now the beast was coming with such a rushing roar that it could ravage a city.

I came near it, and that huge sea monster stretched itself out on the ground and did nothing except thrust out its tongue; it did not move at all until I had passed by it.

Now the beast had four colors on its head: black, then fiery and blood-red, then golden[l][k][j][i][h][g][f][e][d][c], then white.

After I had prayed in the house and sat down on the couch[a], a certain man entered, glorious in appearance, in shepherd’s attire, wearing a white skin, and having a bag on his shoulders and a staff in his hand. And he greeted me, and I returned his greeting.

2. And immediately he sat beside me and says to me, “I have been sent by the most venerable angel, that I may dwell with you for the rest of the days of your life.”

3. I thought that he had come to test me, and I say to him, “Who then are you? For I,” I say, “know the one to whom I was handed over.” He says to me, “Do you not recognize me?” “No,” I say. “I,” he says, “am the Shepherd to whom you were entrusted.”

4. While he was still speaking, his appearance was changed, and I recognized him, that he was the one to whom I had been entrusted, and immediately I was confounded, and fear seized me, and I was completely crushed with grief, because I had answered him so wickedly and senselessly.

5. But he answered me and says, “Do not be confounded, but be strengthened in my mandates, which I am about to command you. For I have been sent,” he says, “that I may show you again all the things you saw before, especially the main points that are beneficial for you. First of all, write my mandates and the parables; but the other things, as I show you, so you will write.” For this reason, he says, “I command you first to write the mandates and parables, so that you may read them readily at hand and be able to keep them.”

6. So I wrote the mandates and the parables, just as he commanded me.

7. If then, having heard them, you keep them and walk in them and do them with a pure heart, you will receive from the Lord what he promised you; but if, having heard, you do not repent[h], but still add to your sins, you will receive from the Lord the opposite things. The Shepherd, the angel of repentance[g][f][e][d][c][b], commanded me to write all these things in this way.

He says to me: Have simplicity[1], and become guileless, and you will be like the little ones who do not know the wickedness that destroys the life of human beings.

First of all, slander no one, and do not listen with pleasure to someone who slanders; otherwise you too, the hearer, will be guilty of the slanderer’s sin if you believe the slander you hear. For by believing it, you yourself also will have something against your brother. Thus you will be guilty of the slanderer’s sin.

Slander is evil; it is a restless demon, never at peace, but always dwelling amid divisions. So keep away from it, and you will always have well‑being with all.

But clothe yourself with dignity, in which there is no evil stumbling block, but all things are smooth and cheerful. Do what is good, and from your labors, which God gives you, give simply to all who are in need, not hesitating as to whom you should give or to whom you should not give. Give to all, for God wants all to be given from his own gifts.

Therefore those who receive will render an account to God why they received and for what; for those who receive while afflicted will not be judged, but those who receive in hypocrisy will pay the penalty.

Therefore the one who gives is innocent[2]; for just as he received from the Lord the ministry to carry out, he carried it out simply, making no distinction as to whom he should give or not give. Thus this ministry, having been carried out simply, became glorious before God. Therefore the one who thus ministers simply to God will live.

So keep this commandment, as I have spoken to you, so that your repentance[b] and that of your household may be found in simplicity[a][7][6][5][4][3], and your heart clean and unstained.

“I am commanding you,” he says[1], “to guard chastity, and do not let a thought about another man’s wife, or about any fornication, or about any such evil likenesses, rise up upon your heart. For in doing this you commit a great sin. But if you remember your own wife always, you will never transgress.

“For if this thought rises up upon your heart, you will transgress—and if other such evil things [do], you commit sin. For this thought is a great sin for a servant of God; and if anyone carries out this evil deed, he brings death upon himself. Look to yourself, then: keep away from this thought; for where modesty dwells, there lawlessness ought not to rise up upon the heart of a righteous man.”

I say to him, “Sir, allow me to ask you a few things.” “Speak,” he says. “Sir,” I say, “if someone has a wife who is faithful in the Lord, and he finds her in some adultery, does the husband sin by living together with her?”

“As long as he is ignorant,” he says, “he does not sin; but if the husband comes to know her sin, and the wife does not repent[b] but persists in her fornication, and the husband lives together with her, he becomes guilty of her sin and a sharer in her adultery. "What then, sir," I say[2], "should the husband do, if the wife persists in this passion?" "Let him divorce her," he says, "and let the husband remain by himself; but if, after divorcing his wife, he marries another, he himself also commits adultery." "If then, sir," I say, "after the wife is divorced, she repents and wishes to return to her own husband, will she not be received?" "Indeed," he says, "if the husband does not receive her, he sins and brings a great sin upon himself; rather, the one who has sinned and is repenting must be received—but not repeatedly—for to the servants of God repentance is one. Because of repentance, then, the man ought not to marry. This rule is laid upon both woman and man.

“Not only,” he says, “is it adultery if someone defiles his flesh, but whoever makes images as the nations do is committing adultery. Therefore, even in such works, if someone persists and does not repent, keep away from him and do not live together with him; otherwise you too are a sharer in his sin. For this reason it was commanded you to remain by yourselves, whether man or woman, for in cases like these there can be repentance.

“I therefore,” he says, “do not give an occasion for this practice to be carried through in this way, but so that the one who has sinned may no longer sin. But with regard to his former sin[a][8][7][6][5][4][3], there is One who is able to give healing—for he is the One who has authority over all.”

I asked him again[1], saying, "Since the Lord has counted me worthy that you should dwell with me always, bear with a few more words from me, since I understand nothing, and my heart has been hardened by my former deeds. Give me understanding, for I am very foolish and altogether perceive nothing."

Answering me, he says, "I," he says, "am over repentance[a], and I give understanding to all who repent. Or does it not seem to you," he says, "that this very thing—to repent—is understanding? To repent," he says, "is great understanding. For the man who has sinned understands that he has done what is evil before the Lord, and the deed that he did comes up upon his heart, and he repents and no longer works the evil, but works the good lavishly[2], and he humbles his own soul and chastises it, because he sinned. You see then that repentance is great understanding."

"For this reason then," I say, "sir, I seek to learn everything exactly from you: first, because I am a sinner; then, because I do not know by doing what works I shall live, for my sins are many and manifold."

"You will live," he says, "if you keep my commandments and walk in them; and whoever, having heard these commandments, keeps them[6][5][4][3], will live to God."

“Still,” I say[1], “sir, I will add another question.”

“Speak,” he says.

“I heard,” I say, “sir, from certain teachers, that there is no other repentance[a] except that one when we went down into the water and received forgiveness of our former sins.”[1][2]

He says to me, “You heard well; for so it is. For the one who has received forgiveness—”[3]

“Bear with me,” I say, “and make this clear to me also.”

“Speak,” he says.

“If a woman,” I say, “sir, or again some man, should fall asleep, and one of them marries[2], does the one who marries sin?”[4]

“He does not sin,” he says; “but if someone remains by himself,[5] he obtains for himself greater honor and great glory with the Lord; but if he also marries, he does not sin. Therefore keep chastity and modesty, and you will live to God. These things that I speak to you and am about to speak, keep from now on, from the day you were entrusted to me, and I will dwell in your house. He says to me: Remove double-mindedness from yourself[a], and do not at all be double-minded when asking anything from God, saying within yourself, “How am I able to ask from the Lord and receive, I who have sinned so much against him?”

Do not reason about these things, but turn to the Lord with your whole heart, and ask from him without doubting; and you will come to know his great tender mercy—for he will certainly not abandon you, but will bring the request of your soul to completion.

For God is not like human beings who remember wrongs; rather, he does not remember wrongs, and he has compassion on what he has made.

Therefore cleanse your heart from all the vanities of this age and from the words previously spoken to you, and ask from the Lord; and you will receive everything, and you will not be left short in any of your petitions, if you ask from the Lord without doubting.

But if you waver in your heart, you will by no means receive anything of your petitions. For those who doubt with respect to God—these are the double-minded—and they do not at all obtain their petitions.

But those who are whole in faith ask for all things, having put their trust in the Lord, and they receive, because they ask without doubting, not being at all double-minded. For every double-minded man, unless he repents[k], will be saved with difficulty.

Cleanse, then, your heart from double-mindedness, and put on faith, because it is strong, and believe God, that all your requests which you ask you will receive. And if ever, after asking some request from the Lord, you receive it more slowly, do not be double-minded because you did not quickly receive the request of your soul; for surely it is because of some testing or some transgression, which you do not know, that you receive your request more slowly.

So do not cease asking for the request of your soul, and you will receive it. But if you grow weary and become double-minded while asking, blame yourself and not the one who gives to you.

Look at this double-mindedness: for it is evil and senseless, and it uproots many from the faith, even those who are very faithful and strong. For this double-mindedness is a daughter of the devil, and it acts very wickedly toward the servants of God.

Therefore despise double-mindedness and master it in every matter, having put on the strong and mighty faith[b]. For faith promises all things and accomplishes all things, but double-mindedness, because it does not trust, fails in all the works that it does.

“You see then,” he says, “that faith is from above, from the Lord, and it has great power; but double-mindedness is an earthly spirit from the devil, having no power.

Therefore serve faith, which has power, and keep away from double-mindedness, which has no power[j][i][h][g][f][e][d][c], and you will live to God—and all who think these things will live to God.”

records.after_text: “Listen, then,” he says, “foolish one, how sorrow wears down[a] the Holy Spirit and again saves. Whenever the double‑minded[b] person sets himself to some deed and fails in it because of his double‑mindedness, this sorrow enters into the person and grieves the Holy Spirit and wears it down. Then again, when quick temper[c] clings to a person about some matter and he becomes exceedingly embittered, again sorrow enters into the heart of the one who gave way to quick temper, and he is grieved over his deed that he did and repents[g], because he worked evil. This sorrow, then, seems to have salvation[f], because having done the evil he repented. Therefore both actions grieve the Spirit: double‑mindedness, because it did not succeed in its deed; and quick temper grieves the Spirit, because it did the evil. Both, then, are grievous to the Holy Spirit—double‑mindedness and quick temper. Remove, therefore, sorrow from yourself, and do not afflict the Holy Spirit that dwells in you, lest it plead[d] with God and depart from you. For the Spirit of God that has been given into this flesh does not endure sorrow or anguish[e].”

1[2]. He showed me men sitting on a bench, and another man sitting on a chair. And he says to me, “Do you see the ones sitting on the bench?” “I see, sir,” I say. “These,” he says, “are faithful; and the one sitting on the chair is a false prophet who destroys the understanding of the servants of God—of the double‑minded, not of the faithful.

2. These, then, the double‑minded, come to him as to a magician and ask him what will happen to them; and that false prophet[4], having in himself no power of a divine spirit, speaks with them according to their questions [and according to the desires of their wickedness], and fills their souls as they desire.

3. For he, being empty, answers empty men with empty things; for whatever he is asked, he answers according to the emptiness of the person. But he also speaks some true words; for the devil fills him with his own spirit, if perhaps he may be able to tear away some of the righteous.

4. Therefore, as many as are strong in the faith of the Lord, having put on the truth, do not cling to such spirits, but keep away from them. But those who are double‑minded and often change their minds[b] practice divination like the nations and bring a greater sin upon themselves by practicing idolatry; for the one who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of the truth and foolish.

5. For no spirit given from God is consulted, but, having the power of the Deity, it speaks everything from itself, because it is from above, from the power of the divine Spirit.

6. But the spirit that is consulted and speaks according to the desires of men is earthly and light, having no power; and it does not speak at all unless it is consulted.

7. “How then,” I say, “sir, will a person know which of them is a prophet and which is a false prophet?” “Listen,” he says, “about both prophets; and in the way I am about to tell you, so you shall test the prophet and the false prophet. Test the man who has the divine spirit by his life.

8. First of all, the one who has the [divine] spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble‑minded, and refrains from every evil and from the vain desire of this age, and makes himself lower than all people; and when consulted he answers nothing to anyone, nor does he speak privately—nor does the holy Spirit speak whenever a person wishes it to speak—but it speaks when God wishes him to speak.

9. Therefore, when the man who has the divine spirit comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit, and an intercession is made to God by the gathering of those men, then the angel of the prophetic spirit who is assigned to him fills the man; and being filled with the holy Spirit he speaks to the multitude as the Lord wills.

10. Thus the spirit of the Deity will be made manifest. As for the spirit of the Deity of the Lord, this is its power.

11. “Hear now,” he says, “about the spirit that is earthly and empty and has no power, but is foolish.

12. First, that man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself and wants to have the first seat; and immediately he is presumptuous and shameless and talkative, and lives among many luxuries and many other deceits, and he receives payment for his prophecy; and if he does not receive it, he does not prophesy. Can a divine spirit receive payment and prophesy? A prophet of God cannot do this; rather, the spirit of such prophets is earthly.

13. Then, he does not come near a gathering of righteous men at all, but avoids them. He clings to the double‑minded and the empty, and he prophesies to them in a corner, and deceives them by speaking everything according to their desires, emptily; for he also answers the empty. For an empty vessel, placed together with empty ones, is not broken, but they agree with one another.

14. [Heaven.] 

19. “How,” I say, “sir, can these things be? For you have said both these things are impossible.” “As these, then, are impossible, so also the spirits that are earthly are impossible and inert.

20. Take now the power that comes from above. Hail is a very small pellet, and when it falls on a man’s head, how much pain it causes! Or again, take a drop that falls from the roof tile to the ground, and it bores through the stone.

21. You see, then, that things from above, though very small when they fall upon the earth, have great power; so also the divine spirit that comes from above is powerful. Trust in this spirit[a][21][14][10][9][8], but keep away from the other.”

But I do not know whether these commandments can be kept by a human being, for they are very hard.

In reply he says to me: “If you set it before yourself that they can be kept, you will keep them easily, and they will not be hard. But if it has already risen up in your heart that they cannot be kept by a human being, you will not keep them.

Now I say to you: if you do not keep these, but only remember them in passing, you will walk in the commandments of the devil—difficult and bitter and savage and licentious. And do not be afraid of the devil, for he has no power against you; for I will be with you—I, the angel of repentance[a]—who has mastery over him. The devil has only fear, and his fear has no strength. Do not therefore be afraid of him, and he will flee from you.”

While I was sitting in my house and glorifying the Lord for all the things I had seen, and pondering the commandments—that they are good and powerful and gladdening and glorious and able to save a person’s soul—I said within myself: “Blessed shall I be if I walk in these commandments, and whoever walks in these will be blessed.”

As I was saying these things within myself, I suddenly see him seated beside me and saying this: “Why are you double-minded about the commandments that I commanded you? They are good. Do not be double-minded at all, but clothe yourself with faith in the Lord, and you will walk in them; for I will strengthen you in them.

“These commandments are beneficial for those who are about to repent[a]; for if they do not walk in them, their repentance is in vain.

“You who are repenting, therefore, throw off the evils of this age that wear you down; and having put on every virtue of righteousness, you will be able to keep these commandments and no longer add to your sins. If, therefore, you add nothing further, you will be separated from your former sins. Walk, therefore, in these my commandments, and you will live to God. These things [all] have been spoken to you by me.”

And after he had spoken these things with me, he says to me, “Let us go into a field, and I will show you the shepherds of the sheep.” “Let us go, sir,” I say. And we came to a certain plain, and he shows me a shepherd, a young man, clothed in a suit of garments, saffron in color.

He was pasturing very many sheep, and the sheep were as if living in luxury and very self-indulgent, and they were cheerful, skipping here and there. And the shepherd himself was very cheerful over his flock; and the very appearance of the shepherd was exceedingly cheerful, and he ran around among the sheep.

And he says to me, “Do you see this shepherd?” “I do,” I say, “sir.”[a]

“Those sheep you saw not skipping but grazing in one place—these are the ones who have handed themselves over to luxuries and deceptions,[b] yet they have not blasphemed the Lord at all.[c] These, then, have been corrupted away from the truth; in them there is hope for repentance[l], by which they can live.[d] Corruption, then, has hope of a certain renewal,[e] but death has eternal destruction.”[f]

5. Again we went on a little, and he shows me a great shepherd, as if savage in appearance, wearing a white goatskin,[g] and he had a bag on his shoulders,[h] and a staff very hard and with knots,[i] and a great whip.[j] He had a very bitter look, so that I was afraid of him—such was his look.[k]

6. This shepherd, then, took over the sheep from the shepherd who was a young man—those that were living profligately and living in self-indulgence, and not skipping—and he cast them into a certain place that was steep, thorny, and full of thistles,[m] so that, because of the thorns and thistles, the sheep were unable to disentangle themselves, but [were entangled in the thorns and thistles; these, then,] being entangled, grazed among the thorns and thistles.[o] They suffered greatly, being beaten by him;[p] he drove them here and there and gave them no rest, and those sheep were not at ease at all.[q]

Therefore[a], seeing them being scourged and harried like this, I was grieved for them, because they were being tormented in this way and had no respite at all. I said to the shepherd who was speaking with me, “Sir, who is this shepherd, so pitiless and harsh, showing no compassion at all for these sheep?” He said, “This is the angel of punishment; he is one of the righteous angels[b], appointed over punishment. Therefore he takes over those who have wandered away from God and have gone after the desires and deceits of this age, and he punishes them, as they deserve, with dreadful and various punishments.”

“I wished, Sir,” I said, “to know what these various punishments are.” He said, “Listen. The various punishments and torments are torments of this present life: for some are punished with losses, some with deprivations, some with various sicknesses, some with every kind of disorder; some are insulted by the unworthy, and suffer in many other undertakings. For many, being unsettled in their plans, take on many projects, and nothing at all advances for them. They say of themselves that they do not prosper in their undertakings, and it does not rise up into their heart that they have done evil, but they blame the Lord.

“When, then, they are pressed by every affliction, then they are handed over to me for good discipline, and they are strengthened in faith in the Lord; and the rest of the days of their life they serve the Lord with a pure heart. And if they repent[j], then the evil works that they did rise up into their heart; and then they glorify God, saying that he is a righteous judge and that each one suffered justly according to his deeds. Thereafter they serve the Lord with a pure heart, and they prosper in every work of theirs, receiving from the Lord whatever they ask for; and then they glorify the Lord because they were handed over to me[i][h][g][f][e][d][c], and they no longer suffer any of the evils.”

“Since,” I say, “sir,[6] I have not understood at all about the time of deception and delight[1] and torment,[2] make it more plain to me.”

He answered me and says, “Your foolishness is persistent, and you are unwilling to cleanse your heart and to serve God. Watch out lest the time be fulfilled, and you be found a fool. Listen then,” he says, “as you desire, so that you may understand these things.

“The person who delights and is deceived for a single day and does what he wants has clothed himself with much foolishness and does not perceive the deed he is doing; for on the next day he forgets what he did the day before. For delight and deception have no memory because of the foolishness with which he has clothed himself. But when punishment and torment cling to a person for one day, he is punished and tormented for up to a year; for punishment and torment have great memory.

“So, being tormented and punished the whole year, he at last[5] remembers the delight and the deception, and he knows that because of them he suffers the evil things. Every person who delights and is deceived is tormented in this way, because, though they had life, they have handed themselves over to death.”

“What delights, sir,” I say, “are harmful?”

He says, “Every deed is a delight to a person, whatever he does with pleasure. For even the hot‑tempered man, by giving his own passion its fill, takes delight; and the adulterer and the drunkard and the slanderer and the liar and the greedy person and the defrauder and the one doing things like these gives his own disease its fill; he therefore delights in his act. All these delights are harmful to the servants of God.[3] Therefore, because of these deceptions, those who are punished and tormented suffer.

“But there are also delights that save people; for many, by doing good things, take delight, being carried along by their own pleasure. This delight, therefore, is beneficial for the servants of God, and it secures life for such a person;[6] but the harmful delights previously mentioned procure torments and punishments for them; and if they persist and do not repent[a],[4] they procure death for themselves.”

1[7]. After a few days I saw him in the same field where I had also seen the shepherds, and he says to me, “What are you seeking?” “I am here, sir,” I say, “that you may command the shepherd, the punisher, to go out from my house, because he afflicts me greatly.” He says, “It is necessary for you to be afflicted; for thus the glorious angel has commanded concerning you, for he wants you to be tested.” “For what, sir,” I say, “have I done that was so evil, that I should be handed over to this angel?”

2. He says, “Listen: your sins are many[a], but not so many that you should be handed over to this angel. Rather, your household has committed great lawless deeds and sins, and the glorious angel was embittered at their works; and for this reason he ordered that you be afflicted for a certain time, so that they too might repent[c] and cleanse themselves from every desire of this age. When therefore they repent and are cleansed, then the angel of punishment will withdraw.”

…with their whole heart[1]. So then, do you suppose that the sins of those who are repenting[b] are immediately forgiven? Not entirely. Rather, the one who repents must afflict his own soul and be humble-minded in all his conduct, resolutely, and be distressed in all kinds of tribulations; and if he bears the tribulations that come upon him, the One who created all things and strengthened them will surely be moved with compassion and will grant some healing. And this, when [God] sees the heart of the one repenting clean from everything.

And an angel of the Lord—exceedingly glorious and very tall—was standing beside the willow, holding a great sickle, and he was cutting off branches from the willow and handing them to the people who were being sheltered by the willow; and he kept giving them little rods, about a cubit long.

After all had received the rods, the angel laid aside the sickle, and that tree was sound, just as I had seen it before. I marveled within myself, saying, How is the tree sound, with so many branches cut off? The shepherd says to me, Do not marvel that the tree remained sound though so many branches were cut off[2]. But wait until you see everything, and it will be shown to you what it is.

The angel who had given the rods to the people again demanded them back from them; and in the order they had received them, so too they were called to him, and each one returned the rods. The angel of the Lord took them and examined them.

From some he received the rods dry and eaten as if by a moth; the angel ordered those who had handed in such rods to stand apart. Others handed in dry rods, but they had not been eaten by a moth; these too he ordered to stand apart. Others handed in rods half-dry; and these stood apart. Others handed in their rods half-dry and having splits; and these stood apart. Others handed in their rods green and having splits; and these stood apart. Others handed in their rods half dry and half green; and these stood apart. Others presented their rods with two parts of the rod green and the third part dry; and these stood apart. Others handed in two parts dry and the third part green; and these stood apart. Others handed in their rods almost entirely green, but a very little of their rods was dry—at the very tip; and they had splits in them[a][5][4][3]; and these stood apart.

I say to him, “Sir, make known to me what this tree is; for I am perplexed about it, because, though so many branches have been cut off, the tree is sound, and nothing appears to have been cut away from it. About this, therefore, I am at a loss.”

“Listen,” he says. “This great tree that covers plains and mountains and the whole earth is the law of God given to the whole world. And this law is the Son of God, proclaimed to the ends of the earth; and the peoples under the shade are those who heard the proclamation and believed in him.[a]

“And the great and glorious angel is Michael, who has authority over this people and governs them. For he is the one who gives the law to them, into the hearts of those who believe; therefore he himself visits those to whom he gave it, to see whether they have kept it.

“You see the rods of each person; for the rods are the law. You see, then, many rods made worthless; and you will recognize all those who have not kept the law, and you will see the dwelling of each one.”[b][c]

I say to him, “Sir, why did he send some away into the tower, but leave others to you?”

“All who transgressed the law which they received from him,” he says, “he left under my authority for repentance[i]; but those who have already been pleasing to the law and have kept it, he has under his own authority.”[d][e]

“Who then, Sir,” I say, “are the ones who are crowned and go into the tower?”

“[Those who grappled with the devil and overcame him,” he says, “are crowned.][f][g] These are the ones who suffered for the law.[h]

“But the others, who themselves also handed in their rods green and having side-shoots, yet without fruit—these are those who were hard-pressed for the law, but did not suffer, nor did they deny their law.

“And those who handed in green rods just as they received them are dignified and righteous and have walked with a very pure heart, and have guarded the commandments of the Lord. The rest you will learn when I examine these rods that have been planted and watered.”

1[1]. The copy of the testament of Asher.

2. In the one hundred and twenty-fifth year of his life, while still healthy, he said to them, “Hear, children of Asher, your father, and I will show you everything upright before God.

3. God has given two ways to the sons of men, and two purposes, and two actions, and two modes, and two outcomes.

4. Therefore all things are twofold[2], set one over against the other.

5. For there are two ways, of good and of evil; and in them are the two purposes in our breasts, distinguishing them.

6. If, then, the soul desires to walk well, it does all its deeds in righteousness; and even if it sins, it immediately repents[a].

7. For by thinking righteous thoughts and casting away wickedness, it at once overturns evil and uproots sin.

8. But if its purpose inclines to evil, all its deeds are in wickedness, driving away the good and clinging to the evil, and it is ruled by Beliar; and even if it does something good, it turns it into evil.

9. For whenever it begins to do good in an evil way, it drives the end of the action for him into evil, because the treasure of its purpose is filled with an evil spirit.

10. My children, obey your father, and bury me near my fathers.”

11. And after he had drawn up his feet, he fell asleep in peace.

12. And after five years they carried him up to Hebron[3], and placed him with his fathers.

records.after_text: Therefore take heed, you also, my children, following the commandments of the Lord with a single face, in truth. For the double-faced are punished doubly, because they both do evil and approve those who do it, imitating the spirits of deceit and contending against mankind. You therefore, my children, keep the law of the Lord, and do not attend to evil as though it were good; but look instead to what is truly good, and preserve it in all the commandments of the Lord, conducting yourselves in it and resting in it. For the ends of men reveal their righteousness, and they are made known to the angels of the Lord and of Beliar. For when a wicked soul departs, it is tormented by the evil spirit, which it also served in lusts and wicked deeds. But if it is peaceful in joy, it knows the angel of peace, and rejoices in him; and at its death he leads it into eternal life. And it does not come into the destruction of Beliar, as do the souls of sinners. You see, therefore, that in the last times the sons of truth will escape the spirits of deceit and Beliar, but the sons of lawlessness will be destroyed. For the latter will hand over their souls to Beliar in confusion, but the former will be found in joy. For every one of those who are double-faced, though he says, 'I am for the Lord,' serves Beliar, and his works go to the evil one. Be persuaded, therefore, my children, that there are two ways of all things, one of good and one of evil; and in these are the two dispositions in our breasts that discern them. Therefore if the soul takes pleasure in the good, all its deeds are in righteousness; and if it sins, it immediately repents[a]. For, having its mind set on righteousness and hating wickedness, it casts away the evil and roots out the sin. But if it inclines to evil, all its deeds are in wickedness, and it drives away the good and clings to the evil, and is ruled by Beliar. For even if it does what is good, it twists it toward evil. For when it begins to do good, it brings the end of the action over to evil, since the treasure of its inclination is filled with an evil spirit. Another may steal, deal unjustly, plunder, defraud, and yet show compassion to the poor: this too has a double face, but the whole is evil. He who defrauds his neighbor provokes God, and swears falsely by the Most High, and yet has pity on the poor. The Lord who gave the law he sets at naught and provokes, yet he refreshes the poor. He defiles the soul and makes the body glad; he kills many and has mercy on a few: this too has a double face. Another does not commit adultery, nor fornication, and abstains from foods, but when he fasts he does evil, and by his power and his wealth he overthrows many; and despite his excessive goodness, he practices lawlessness: this too has a double face. Such men are hares, clean like those that divide the hoof, but in fact they are unclean. For God said in the tablets of the commandments. But do not become, my children, like Sodom, which did not recognize the angels of the Lord and perished forever. For I know that you will sin, and be handed over into the hands of your enemies; and your land will be made desolate, and your holy places destroyed, and you will be scattered to the four corners of the earth. And you will be counted in the dispersion as water that vanishes, until the Most High visits the earth, himself coming as a man, with men eating and drinking, and breaking the head of the dragon in the water. He will save Israel and all the nations, God speaking in the person of man. Therefore tell these things to your children also, that they may disobey him. For I know that they will surely be lawless and will not heed the law of God, but the commandments of men; and they will be scattered as leaves are scattered by the wind, and as water is dispersed. But you, my children, if you walk in holiness according to the commandments of the Lord, you will dwell again in safety, and all Israel will be gathered to the Lord.

1[a]. The copy of the words of Gad, what things he spoke to his sons in the hundred and twenty-fifth year of his life, saying to them:
2. Listen to the words of truth, my children, and practice righteousness and all the law of the Most High. Do not go astray after the spirit of hatred, for it is evil in all the deeds of men.
3. Whatever a man hates, that he does not want to see or hear. If anyone speaks of the Lord, he hates him as one who reproves him. If anyone prospers, he envies him. If anyone is rich, he is not pleased with it. If anyone is brave, he praises him not. He slanders a truthful man, he begrudges a successful man, and he loves the arrogant and the lawless. For hatred blinds his soul, as I also saw concerning Joseph.
4. For I began to hate him from the day when he told our father that the sons of Zilpah and Bilhah were slaughtering the best of the flock and eating them apart from Judah and Joseph.
5. For he told our father that I had said, “I saw a lamb being torn by a bear, and while I was running after the bear I killed it; but the lamb I slaughtered, because it could not live, and we ate it.”
6. And because of this I was angry with Joseph until the day he was sold.
7. And the spirit of hatred was in me, and I did not want either to hear Joseph with my ears or to see him with my eyes, because he rebuked us to our face, saying that we were eating the flock without Judah.
8. For everything that he told our father, he believed.
9. I confess now my sin, my children, that many times I wanted to kill him, because I hated him from my heart.
10. And I hated him still more because of his dreams; and I wanted to destroy him from the earth[b], just as an ox devours the grass of the field.
11. Therefore I and Judah sold him to the Ishmaelites for thirty pieces of gold.
12. But the Lord of our fathers did not allow us to deal lawlessly with him, so that we should kill him.
13. And now, my children, I tell you: love each one his brother, and put away hatred from your hearts. Love one another in deed and in word and in the disposition of the soul.
14. For in the presence of my father I spoke peaceably to Joseph, but when I had gone out, the spirit of hatred darkened my mind and stirred up my soul to kill him.
15. Love one another from the heart; and if a man sins against you, speak peaceably to him, and in your soul hold no deceit; and if he confesses and repents[e], forgive him.
16. But if he denies it, do not become heated with him, lest by taking in the poison from him you swear and so sin doubly.
17. Let no one hear your secrets when he is quarreling with you, lest he hate you and become your enemy and commit some great sin against you; for often he speaks craftily with you, or keeps company with you for an evil end.
18. And if he denies it and is ashamed when reproved, be quiet. For by denying it he repents, and he will no longer wrong you; indeed he will honor you and fear you and be at peace with you.
19. But if he is shameless and persists in his wrongdoing, even so forgive him from the heart, and leave vengeance to God.
20. If anyone becomes rich by unjust means, do not envy him; but wait for the end appointed by the Lord.
21. For if he takes away and gives back double, do not be troubled; but be patient until the Lord executes judgment.
22. For the poor man, if free from envy, is pleasing to the Lord in all things, and is blessed beyond all men, because he does not have the toil of vain men.
23. Therefore put envy away from your souls, and love one another with uprightness of heart.
24. Tell these things also to your children, that they may honor Levi and Judah; for from them the Lord will raise up salvation for Israel.
25. For I know that at the last you will depart from him and walk lawlessly and do violence to Levi and fight against Judah.
26. But you will not prevail against them, because an angel of the Lord guides them both; for by them Israel will stand.
27. And when you depart from the Lord, you will walk in every evil deed and commit the abominations of the nations, going astray after women who practice lawlessness, while spirits of wickedness work in you with every malice.
28. For I have read in the book of Enoch the righteous that your prince is Satan, and that all the spirits of sexual immorality and arrogance will attend on the sons of Levi, to cause them to sin before the Lord.
29. And my sons will draw near to Levi and sin with them in all things; and the sons of Judah will be greedy, plundering other men's goods like lions.
30. Therefore you will be led away with them into captivity, and there you will receive all the plagues of Egypt and all the evils of the nations.
31. Therefore, when you return to the Lord, act in uprightness and all righteousness, and deal mercy and truth each one with his neighbor.
32. And if you return to the Lord with uprightness of heart, and put away hatred and lawlessness, and love one another from the heart, then there will be peace for you.
33. And no son of man will be able to prevail against you, because the God of heaven will be among you, making peace for you and for all Israel.
34. And no enemy will rejoice over you; and every wild beast will fear you, and the Lord will bless you in every work and in every word.
35. And now, my children, fear the Lord God of heaven, and beware of Satan and his spirits.
36. Draw near to God and to the angel who intercedes for you, for he is a mediator between God and men for the peace of Israel.
37. He will stand against the kingdom of the enemy; therefore the enemy is eager to destroy all who call on the Lord.
38. For he knows that on the day when Israel repents, the kingdom of the enemy will be brought to an end.
39. For the very angel of peace will strengthen Israel, so that it may not fall into the extremity of evil.

1[a]. And now, my children, I urge you: let each one love his neighbor, and remove hatred from your hearts. Love one another in deed and word and with the intention of the soul.

2. For I myself, in my father’s presence, spoke peaceably to Joseph; but when I went out from his presence, the spirit of hatred darkened my mind and disturbed my understanding so that I wanted to kill him.

3. Love one another from the heart; and if anyone sins against you[b], speak peace to him, and in your soul hold no deceit; and if he confesses and changes his mind, forgive him.

5. Do not let a stranger hear your secret in a quarrel, lest, hating you, he become your enemy and commit a great sin against you; for many times he either kills by treachery or entangles you in evils, having taken in from you the poison.

6. But if he denies it and is ashamed when reproved, be still and do not reprove him further. For the one who denies it repents[d] of having done wrong against you, so as not to wrong you again, and, being afraid, makes peace.

7. But even if he is shameless and persists in his wrongdoing, even so forgive him from the heart[c], and leave vengeance to God.

Say these things[a], you also, to your children:

that they honor Levi and Judah; for from them the Lord will raise up salvation for Israel.
And tell them concerning Joseph, that they should love him, because in every affliction he was innocent,
and he kept the commandment of God, not returning evil for evil.
For he suffered much from his brothers, yet he loved them,
and though they plotted against him, he spoke peaceably to them.

And now, my children, I command you: love one another from the heart,
and if anyone sins against you, speak peaceably to him, and in your soul hold no deceit;
and if he confesses and repents[d], forgive him.
But if he denies it, do not become heated in argument with him,
lest, after taking in poison[b], he begin to swear and so commit a double sin.
If anyone prospers beyond you, do not be grieved;
but pray also for him, that he may be made complete in every good thing.

If anyone is glorified, do not envy him;
if anyone is enriched, do not be jealous.
Bless the Lord who gives good things to all,
because the poor man, if he is free from envy, is rich before the Lord.
Do not hate a beautiful woman because of her appearance,
and do not hate a man because of the abundance of his glory.
For God gives the good things of the earth to whom he wills.

Seek uprightness in your own works,
and pray for your neighbor, so that if he prospers in every good thing, you may not be jealous.
For the one who is jealous is always in turmoil,
and the one who hates is always darkened.
Love one another in deed and in word and in the intention of the soul.
For I also spoke peaceably with Joseph, but in my heart I intended to kill him.
The spirit of hatred is evil, because it is never at peace with men;
it always desires their downfall.
It weakens the body and disturbs the soul,
and it puts wrath upon the mind.

Therefore, if anyone does evil to you, do good to him,
and pray for him; and you will be redeemed by the Lord from every evil.
For if anyone prospers, and if he is shameless or lawless, do not be jealous;
but wait for the end from the Lord.
For either he receives his reward in this life,
or, if he is kept for punishment, he will be repaid in the judgment.
And if a poor man prospers and is without envy, even if he is not rich,
he is blessed beyond all men, because he has the treasure that does not perish.
Therefore cast away hatred[c], and love one another in uprightness of heart.

1[a]. And while I was there, the king of Adullam, Barshaba, dealt hospitably with us and made us a drinking feast; and when he urged me, he gave me his daughter, whose name was Shua, as a wife.

2. She bore me Er and Onan and Shelah. And the Lord killed the first two, for Er was wicked; and Onan, when he had married Tamar, spilled the seed upon the ground, according to the commandment of his mother, and he also died through wickedness.

3. And Shelah lived, and I did not give Tamar to him as wife. For I said, “Lest he also die like his brothers.” For I did not know that the Lord was judging me because of the things I had done at Timnah to my father Jacob and to Joseph.

4. And after these things, while Tamar was a widow, and after two years had passed, there was reported to me that she was going up to shear sheep at Timnah. And I also went to shear my sheep.

5. And she, having learned that I was going up, adorned herself in bridal array and sat in the city Enaim by the gate. For it was a law of the Amorites that she who was about to marry should sit for seven days by the gate in fornication.

6. Therefore, being drunk with wine, I did not recognize her; and her beauty led my mind astray through the fashion of her adornment.

7. And I turned aside to her and said, “Let me go in to you.” And she said, “What will you give me, that you may come in to me?”

8[b]. And I said, “I will send you a kid from the flock.” And she said, “Will you give me a pledge until you send it?”

9. And I said, “What pledge shall I give you?” And she said, “Your staff, and your girdle, and the diadem of your kingdom.”

10. So I gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by me. And because of the wine I did not perceive what I had done; neither did I recognize her when I went away.

11. And after this I sent the kid, but I did not find her. And I asked the people of the place, saying, “Where is the woman who sat at Enaim by the road?”

12. And they said, “There has been no prostitute here, nor any stranger sitting by the gate.” And I understood that I had sinned, and I did not make the matter known publicly, because I was ashamed.

13. And after three months it was reported to me, “Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the prostitute, and behold, she is with child.” And I, being without understanding in the arrogance of my anger, said, “Bring her out, and let her be burned.”

14. But as she was being brought out, she sent secretly to me the staff and the girdle and the diadem, saying, “By the man to whom these belong I am with child.”

15. And I recognized them and was ashamed, and I said, “Tamar is more righteous than I, because I did not give her to Shelah my son.” And I did not know her again.

16. And now, my children, I say to you: do not be drunk with wine. For wine turns the mind away from the truth and inspires the passion of desire, and it leads the eyes into error.

17. For the spirit of sexual immorality has wine as a servant to give pleasure to the mind; for these two also take away a person’s understanding.

18. For if one drinks wine to drunkenness, it disturbs the mind with filthy thoughts and leads the body on to sexual union; and if the occasion of desire is present, he commits the sin and is not ashamed.

19. Such is the drunkard, my children. For the one who is drunk does not reverence anyone. For behold, it made me also transgress the commandment of God, and I went in to Tamar, not being ashamed of the multitude in the city, and before the eyes of all I uncovered the shame of my sons, since I went in to Tamar.

20. After I had drunk wine, I did not respect the commandment of God, and I took a woman of Canaan as wife. For much discretion is needed by the man who drinks wine, my children.

21. And this is the discretion in drinking wine: if a man drinks wine and keeps modesty, and if he does not go astray into shamelessness, he may drink wine.

22. But if he goes beyond the limit, the spirit of deceit attacks his mind and makes the drunkard speak obscenities and transgress, and not be ashamed, but even boast in his disgrace and count it glory.

23. One who commits sexual immorality does not know when he suffers loss, and he is not ashamed when dishonored. For even if a man is a king and commits sexual immorality, he is stripped of his kingship by becoming a servant to sexual immorality, as I myself also suffered.

24. For I gave my staff, that is, the stay of my tribe; and my girdle, that is, my power; and my diadem, that is, the glory of my kingdom.

25. And indeed I repented[f] of these things; and wine and meat I did not consume until old age, and I saw no joy.

26. And the angel of God showed me that women rule forever over king and beggar alike. From a king they take away his glory, and from a strong man his strength, and from a beggar even the little support of his poverty.

27. Therefore keep yourselves, my children, from sexual immorality and from the love of money, and listen to Judah your father.

28. For these things draw a person away from the law of God and blind the inclination of the soul, and teach arrogance, and do not allow one to have compassion on his neighbor.

29. They deprive his soul of every goodness and oppress him with toils and troubles, and drive sleep away from him and devour his flesh.

30. And he is hindered from offering sacrifices to God; and he does not remember blessing God; and when he hears a prophet speaking, he is offended and angered.

31. For he is enslaved to two contrary passions and cannot obey God, because they have blinded his soul and he walks in the day as in the night.

32. My children, I have shown you that wine leads to sexual immorality, and the love of money to idolatry; and these things turn the mind away from the law of God.

33. Therefore, if you do not walk in sobriety in truth and in the fear of God, you will perish through every evil deed and every plague, if you take wives from the daughters of Canaan and are joined to their wealth, being led astray by gifts.

34. For I know that after my death you will act lawlessly and contend against Levi, and you will not be able to prevail against him, because the angel of the Lord guides him and me the spirit of deceit has misled.

35. And now I command you to love Levi, that you may live, and do not exalt yourselves against him, lest you be utterly destroyed.

36. For to me the Lord gave the kingship, and to him the priesthood; and he set the kingdom under the priesthood.

37. To me he gave the things on earth; to him the things in heaven.

38. As heaven is higher than earth, so is the priesthood of God higher than the earthly kingdom—unless it falls away through sin from the Lord and is dominated by the earthly kingdom.

39. For the angel of the Lord said to me, “The Lord chose Levi before you, to be near him, and for you to be king with him, as a lion.”

40. Therefore be not lifted up over Levi, nor against me, but honor in full the Lord in both, and among men draw near to Levi.

41. For because of him the Lord will choose from you the kingship, and from Levi the priesthood, that the Lord may be for all the nations and the race of Israel.

42. And now I have commanded you these things, because I have read in the books of Enoch the righteous that your sons will turn away from the Lord[c][d][e], and will commit every wickedness and every affliction before the Lord.

2 Two years after the death of Joseph his brother, when Reuben had fallen sick, the sons of Joseph and the sons of his sons were gathered to visit him. 3 And he said to them, “My children, behold, I am dying, and I am going the way of my fathers.” 4 Then, seeing there Judah and Gad and Asher, his brothers, he said to them, “Raise me up, so that I may tell my brothers and my children the things hidden in my heart; for behold, even now I am failing.” 5 And rising up, he kissed them and said to them, “Hear, my brothers and my sons; pay attention to Reuben your father in the things that I command you.

6 “And behold, today I call the God of heaven to witness against you, that you not walk in the ignorance of youth and in sexual immorality, in which I was poured out and defiled the bed of my father Jacob. 7 And I tell you that he struck me with a severe blow in my loins for seven months; and if my father Jacob had not prayed for me to the Lord, the Lord would have been willing to destroy me. 8 For I was thirty years old when I did the evil thing before the Lord, and for seven months I was weakened to the point of death. 9 And after this, with the resolve of my soul, I repented[a] before the Lord for seven years. 10 And I drank no wine or strong drink, and meat did not enter my mouth, and I ate no bread of desire; but I was mourning over my sin, for it was great—such a thing had not happened in Israel.”

And now, my children, hear me concerning what I saw about the seven spirits of deceit[a] in my repentance[d]. There were given, then, seven spirits set against man, and these are the heads of the works of youthfulness[b].

And seven other spirits were given to him at creation, so that every work of man might be in them. The first is the spirit of life, by which a person’s constitution is formed. The second is the spirit of sight, by which desire comes to be. The third is the spirit of hearing, by which instruction comes to be. The fourth is the spirit of smell, by which tastes are produced for the drawing in of air and breath[c]. The fifth is the spirit of speech, by which knowledge comes to be. The sixth is the spirit of taste, by which the eating of foods and drinks comes to be, and strength is formed by it, because in foods is the basis of strength. The seventh is the spirit of procreation and intercourse, by which sins come together through the love of pleasure. Therefore this spirit is last in creation and first in youth, because it is filled with ignorance, and it leads the young man like a blind man into a pit, and like an animal over a cliff.

After he had been thrown into the pit[a], my brothers sat down to eat and drink. But I, having compassion for Joseph, did not eat; for I kept watch by the pit, because Judah feared that Simeon and Gad might leap up and kill him. And when they saw that I also was not eating, they set me to guard him until he was sold. He spent three days and three nights in the pit, and so he was sold while fasting.

When Reuben came and heard that he had been sold while he was away, he tore his garments and mourned, saying, “How shall I look upon the face of my father Jacob?” And taking the silver, he ran after the merchants, but found no one; for they had left the main road and gone by a shorter route through the Troglodytes. Reuben was grieved, and on that day he ate no bread.

Then Dan came up to him and said, “Do not weep or be distressed; for we have found what we shall say to our father. Let us slaughter a male goat with the sword, stain Joseph’s tunic, and send it to Jacob our father, saying, ‘Look whether this is the tunic of your son.’” And they did so. Therefore Jacob bewailed Joseph all his days.

And my brothers were afraid, and they all repented[h] because of what they had done to Joseph. But the Egyptians and the Ishmaelites did him no harm, because the Lord did not allow them to do evil to him.

For he was a handsome man, good-looking and beautiful in appearance, and there was no spite in him, but he was gentle and had a simple soul. Therefore be compassionate, my children[b], because compassion is good for all. And mercy, even if a man is a sinner, if he has compassion, the Lord will count it as righteousness for him. And even if he prospers, if he has no compassion, the Lord will destroy him.

For in the days of famine I remembered the compassion of the Lord, and I gave to all the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow. And when I was forty years old, I took a wife, for my life had been spent in toil and labor, and because of my simplicity I had no wealth. For my father had blessed me, saying, “Your sons shall be like a haven for sailors, and like a harbor for ships.”

And now, my children, I command you: have compassion toward every man with mercy, so that the Lord also may have compassion on you. Because in the last days you will depart from the Lord, and you will provoke Levi to anger, and you will rise up against Judah; but you will not prevail against them, for an angel of the Lord will guide them both, because by them Israel will stand.

And whenever you depart from the Lord, you will walk in every evil and commit the abominations of the nations, going astray after women and being enslaved by every wickedness while the spirits of deceit work in you. For I have read in the writing of Enoch that your sons also will be corrupted in the last days, and will commit lawlessness against the sons of Levi, and will sin against Judah. But they will not be able to stand against them; for from Levi the Lord will raise up a priest, and from Judah a king, God and man. He will save all the nations and the race of Israel.

And now I command you, my children: obey Zebulun your father, and have mercy on your neighbors, and compassion on all, not only on men, but also on the cattle. For because of this the Lord blessed me, and when all my brothers were sick, I remained without sickness; for the Lord knows the intention of each man.

Have compassion, therefore, in your inward parts, my children, because in whatever way a man does to his neighbor, so also the Lord will do to him. For I saw the sons of my brothers sickening and dying because they had no compassion; but my sons were kept unharmed, as you know. For in the days of Canaan I made no gain from a balance of weights, nor did I have in my house a double measure, but all my possessions were shared with all in singleness of heart. And I did not remember evil against anyone. Even to the age of old age I kept my integrity in all things.

You also, therefore, my children, keep the law of the Lord, and show mercy to your neighbor, and deal compassionately with all, not only with men but also with irrational animals. Because of this also I found mercy with the Lord, and all men blessed me, and the Lord increased my goods a thousandfold. For the compassionate man does good to his own soul.

Know, therefore, my children, that in the last times you will depart from the Lord, and you will be divided in Israel, and you will follow two evils, and you will not be found in the assembly of the righteous. But after these things the Lord himself will arise for you, the light of righteousness, and he will heal and save all. And he will bring back the captives from Beliar, and he will turn disobedient hearts to the Lord, and he will grant everlasting peace to those who call on him.

And the saints shall rest in Eden, and in the New Jerusalem the righteous shall rejoice, and it shall be for the glory of God forever. And Jerusalem shall no longer endure desolation, nor shall Israel be led captive; for the Lord will be in her midst, dwelling among men, and the Holy One of Israel will reign over them in humility and poverty. And whoever believes in him shall reign in truth in the heavens.

And now, my children, fear the Lord your God, and beware of Satan and his spirits. Draw near to God and to the angel who intercedes for you, for he is a mediator between God and men for the peace of Israel. He will stand against the kingdom of the enemy; therefore the enemy is eager to destroy all who call on the Lord. For he knows that on the day when Israel repents, the kingdom of the enemy will be brought to an end.

For the angel of peace himself will strengthen Israel, so that it may not fall into the extremity of evil. And in the time of Israel’s lawlessness the Lord will not abandon them, but will transform them into a nation that does his will; for no angel is equal to him. His name is in every place in Israel and among the nations.

Keep yourselves, therefore, from every evil deed, and cast away hatred and every deceit, and love one another in truth and with patience. And the things that I have heard from my father, hand on to your children, so that the Savior of the nations may receive you; for he is gentle and humble, and by his own example he teaches the law of God.

Flee, therefore, from all unrighteousness, and cling to the righteousness of the law of the Lord, and your seed will be forever, and you will be blessed in all your generations.

…the times are near and already closing in. The pitcher is near the well, the ship is near the harbor, the journey is near the city, and life is near its end.

records.after_text:
So while we are still on earth, let us repent[b], because we are like clay in the hands of a craftsman.

When a potter is making a container and it becomes misshapen or crushed in his hands, he shapes it again. But once he has put it into the fiery oven, he can no longer repair it. In the same way, while we are still in this world, let us repent wholeheartedly of the evil things we have done with our bodies, so that we may be saved by the Lord while we still have time to repent.

After we leave this world, we can no longer confess our sins or repent.

Therefore, brothers and sisters, if we do the Father’s will, keep our bodies pure, and obey the Lord’s commands, we will receive eternal life.

For the Lord says in the Gospel, “If you have not kept what is small, who will entrust you with something great? I tell you, whoever is faithful in the smallest matter is also faithful in much.”

This is what he means: “Keep your body pure and the seal unstained,[a] so that we may receive life.”

None of you should say that this body will not be judged or raised from the dead.

Think about it: What body were you in when you were saved? What body were you in when you received your sight? It was this body.

So we must care for our bodies as temples of God. Just as you were called while you were in the body, you will also come in the body.

Christ the Lord, who saved us, was first spirit and then became flesh, and he called us in that way. In the same way, we too will receive our reward in this body.

So let us love one another, so that we may all enter God’s kingdom.

While there is still time for us to be healed, let us put ourselves in the hands of God, our physician, and give him something in return. What can we give him? Sincere, heartfelt repentance[a].

He knows all things beforehand and knows what is in our hearts. So let us praise him forever, not only with our lips but also from our hearts, so that he may receive us as sons.

For the Lord also said, “Those who do the will of my Father are my brothers.”

Therefore, brothers and sisters, let us repent[b] now. Let us think clearly about what is good, because we are full of foolishness and evil. Let us wipe away the sins of our past. We must not live merely to win people’s approval. Let us seek to please not only one another, but also people outside the church by living rightly, so that God’s Name is not dishonored because of us.

For the Lord says, “People among the nations speak evil of my Name everywhere.” He also says, “How terrible it will be for the person who causes my Name to be spoken against!” How do people speak against it? They do so because you do not obey what I desire.

When people outside the church hear us speak God’s messages, they are amazed at their beauty and greatness. But when they discover that our lives do not match our words, they quickly speak evil of God’s message, calling it an empty tale and a deception.

They hear us say that God teaches, “There is nothing praiseworthy about loving those who love you. What is praiseworthy is loving your enemies and those who hate you.” They are amazed at how good this teaching is. But when they see that we fail to show such love,[a] they ridicule us, and God’s Name is dishonored.

Therefore, brothers and sisters, we have a great opportunity to repent[a]. While there is still time, let us return to God who called us, while he still receives us.

If we turn away from these pleasures and master our own desires by refusing to satisfy their evil cravings, we will share in Jesus’ mercy.

But you know that the day of judgment is already coming like a blazing furnace. The powers of heaven will melt, and the whole earth will melt like lead in a fire. Then everything people have done, whether secret or public, will be revealed.

Therefore, let us repent[a] wholeheartedly, so that none of us is lost along the way. We have been commanded to make it our concern to draw people away from idols and teach them. How much worse, then, for someone who already knows God to be lost!

So let us help one another. Let us help those who are weak rise toward what is good, so that we may all be saved. Let us help one another turn back and warn one another.

We must not think that we need to listen and believe only while we are here. After we go home, let us remember the Lord’s commandments. We must not let our worldly desires drag us in the opposite direction. Instead, let us come here more often and work to make progress in obeying the Lord’s commandments. Then, united in mind, we may be gathered together into life.

For the Lord said, “I am coming to gather all nations, tribes, and languages.” This refers to the day when he appears. He will come and redeem us, dealing with each person according to what that person has done.

Those who did not believe will see his glory and power. They will be stunned when they see the kingdom of the world given to Jesus. They will say, “How terrible for us! You were, but we did not know you or believe. We did not obey the elders when they told us about our salvation.” And Scripture says, “Their worm will not die, their fire will not be put out, and they will be displayed before all humanity.”

This speaks of the day of judgment. Then people will see those among us who lived godless lives and were unfaithful to the commandments of Jesus Christ.

The righteous have done good, endured suffering, and rejected the pleasures of the soul. They will see those who did wrong and denied Jesus by their words or actions suffering severe punishment in fire that cannot be put out. Then the righteous will give glory to God and say, “There will be hope for anyone who has served God wholeheartedly.”
