1. I also asked the Savior, “Lord, will all souls be brought safely into the pure light?”

2. He answered, “You are thinking about profound matters. They are difficult to explain to anyone except those who belong to the unmoving race.

3. The Spirit of life will rest on some people and give them power. They will be saved and made perfect. They will be worthy of the Greatness. There they will be cleansed from all evil and from taking part in evil.

4. From then on, their only concern will be indestructibility. They will set their minds on it, without anger, envy, jealousy, lust, or greed for anything. Nothing will trouble them except the burden of living in the flesh. They will endure it as they eagerly wait for those appointed to receive them.

5. Such people are worthy of indestructible, eternal life and of being chosen. They stand firm and endure everything so that they may finish the contest and inherit eternal life.”

6. I asked him, “Lord, what about those on whom the power and the Spirit of life descended, but who did not do these things? Will their souls be rejected?”

7. He answered, “If the Spirit descended on them, they will still be saved, and they will change their ways. The power will descend on all people, because no one can endure without it.

8. After they are born, the Spirit of life increases in them, and the power comes and strengthens their souls. Then no one will be able to lead them astray into evil deeds.

9. But those on whom the false spirit descends are dragged away and led astray by it.”

10. I asked, “Lord, when their souls leave their bodies, where will they go?”

11. He grinned and said to me, “The soul in which the power becomes stronger than the vile spirit—because that soul is strong and flees from evil—will be saved through the intervention of the indestructible one and raised to the resting place of the eternal ages.”

12. I asked, “Lord, where will the souls live if they did not know the one to whom they belong?”

13. He said to me, “When the vile spirit becomes strong in them, they go astray. It weighs down the soul and drags it into evil deeds. It throws the soul down into forgetfulness. After the soul leaves the body, it is handed over to the authorities who came from the archon, the ruling power. They bind it with chains, throw it into prison, and keep watch over it until it awakens from forgetfulness and gains knowledge. If it is made perfect in this way, it will be saved.”

14. I asked, “Lord, how can the soul become smaller and return to the natural state of its mother or into the man?”

15. He rejoiced at my question and said, “You are truly blessed, because you have understood that such a soul will be made to come after another person in whom the Spirit of life dwells.

16. It will be saved through that person.

17. It will not be thrown into another body again.”

18. I also asked, “Lord, where will the souls go if they knew but then turned away?”

19. He said to me, “They will be taken to the place where the angels of destitution go, a place where there is no repentance[a]. They will be held there until the day when those who have blasphemed the Spirit are tormented. They will receive punishment lasting an age.”

records.after_text:
I will also tell you about the temple. These miserable people were led astray. They put their hope in the building instead of in the God who created them, as though the building itself were truly God’s house.

They treated God almost as the Gentiles treated their gods, as though he belonged inside the temple. But listen to what the Lord says as he sets the temple aside: “Who measured the heavens with the span of his hand, or measured the earth with his hand? Was it not I?” says the Lord. “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house could you build for me? Where could I rest?” You can see that their hope was empty.

He also says, “Look! Those who tore down this temple will themselves rebuild it.”

And that is what happens. Because the people went to war, their enemies tore the temple down. Now even servants of those enemies will rebuild it.

It was also revealed that the city, the temple, and the people of Israel would be handed over. Scripture says, “In the last days, the Lord will hand over the sheep of the pasture, along with their fold and its tower, to be destroyed.” This happened just as the Lord had said.

But let us ask whether there is a temple of God. There is: it is where God himself will make and complete it. For it is written, “When the week has run its course, the temple of God will be built in glory in the name of the Lord.”

So I find that there is a temple. But how will it be built in the name of the Lord? Understand this: before we believed in God, the inner dwelling of our hearts was corrupt and weak. It was truly a temple made by human hands, full of idolatry and inhabited by demons, because we did everything that opposed God.

But this temple will be built in the name of the Lord. Pay attention, then, so that the Lord’s temple may be built in glory.

How does this happen? Understand: by receiving forgiveness for our sins and putting our hope in the Lord’s name, we were made new—created all over again. Therefore God truly lives within us. How does he live in us? By the word of his faith, the call of his promise, the wisdom of his ordinances, and the commands of his teaching. God himself prophesies in us and lives within us. We had been enslaved to death, but he opens the temple’s door—our mouth—and gives us repentance[a]. In this way he leads us to the temple that can never decay.

Anyone who wants to be saved does not focus on the person who is speaking, but on God, who lives and speaks within that person. The hearer is amazed because he has never before heard such words from that speaker’s mouth, and he himself had never even wanted to hear them. This is the spiritual temple being built for the Lord.

records.after_text:
Long ago, wise people spoke of the soul as feminine. The soul is indeed female by nature and even has a womb.

As long as she lived alone with the Father, she was a virgin, though her form was both male and female. But when she fell into a body and entered this life, she fell into the hands of many robbers. These cruel beings passed her from one to another and [violated] her.[a] Some took her by force, while others seduced her with gifts. In short, they defiled her, and she [lost] her virginity.

While in the body, she lived as a prostitute and gave herself to everyone. She regarded each one she embraced as her husband. After surrendering herself to cruel and unfaithful adulterers who abused her, she groaned deeply and repented[b].

But even when she turned away from those adulterers, she ran to others. They forced her to live with them and serve them in their beds as though they were her masters. She was so ashamed that she no longer dared to leave. For a long time they deceived her by pretending to be faithful, true husbands who deeply honored her. After all this, they abandoned her and went away.

Then she became a helpless, poor, abandoned widow. In her distress, she did not have even a morsel of food. All she received from them was the uncleanness that came from sexual intercourse. The children she bore to these adulterers could not speak or see; they were sickly and unable to understand.

Then the exalted Father visited her and looked upon her. He saw her groaning in pain and shame and repenting of her prostitution. She began to call on his name for help. Groaning with all her heart, she said, “Save me, my Father. Look upon me, for I will give [an account to you]. I abandoned my home and fled from my maiden’s room. Bring me back to yourself once more.”

When he sees her in this condition, he will decide that she is worthy to receive his mercy, because she has suffered greatly since abandoning her home.

records.reference: Exegesis on the Soul — The Restoration of the Soul
records.rationale: Restore repentance in the souls return, preserving its explicit sorrow, confession and distinctive allegory; this is English-witness editing, not fresh ancient-language certification.
records.after_text:
But when she recognizes her trouble, cries out to the Father, and repents[a], the Father will have mercy on her. He will turn her womb away from the outward kingdom and back inward. In this way, the soul recovers her good character. A woman’s physical womb is not outward; it is inside her body with her other organs.

The soul’s womb, however, surrounds her outwardly, like a man’s external genitals. When the Father wills the soul’s womb to turn inward, it is baptized. At once it is cleansed from the outward pollution forced upon it. It is like filthy [garments] soaked [in water and] shaken about until all the dirt is gone and they are clean. The soul’s cleansing restores and renews her former nature; she returns to herself. This is her baptism.

Then she will become angry with herself. She will be like a woman in labor, twisting and raging when the time comes to give birth. Yet because she is female, she cannot conceive a child by herself. The Father sent her a man from heaven—her brother, the firstborn. The bridegroom came down to the bride.

She gave up her former prostitution and cleansed herself from the pollution of her adulterous partners. She was renewed to become a bride. She cleansed herself in the bridal chamber, filled it with perfume, and sat there waiting for her true bridegroom. She no longer wandered through the marketplace, having sex with anyone she wanted. Instead, she kept waiting for him and asking, “When will he come?” She was still afraid of him because she did not know what he looked like. She no longer remembered when she had fallen from her Father’s house. By the will of the Father, however, [. . .] She dreamed about him like a woman in love with a man.

Then the bridegroom, in accordance with the Father’s will, came down to her, entered the bridal chamber she had prepared, and adorned it.

Therefore, we should pray to the Father and call on him with our whole soul. Our sighs should not come merely from our lips, but from the spirit deep within us. We must turn away from our former way of life, confess our sins, and recognize that the life we lived was an empty lie and that our zeal was hollow. We must mourn because darkness and a wave have swept over us. We must weep over ourselves so that he may have compassion on us, hating what we have now become.

The Savior also said:

“Blessed are those who mourn,
for they will be shown pity.
Blessed are those who hunger,
for they will be filled.”
(Matthew 5:4, 6; Luke 6:21)

He also said, “If someone does not hate his own soul, he cannot follow me.” (Luke 14:26)

This is because repentance[b] is the beginning of salvation. That is why Scripture says, “Before Christ appeared, John came preaching a baptism of repentance.” (Acts 13:24)

Repentance comes with pain and sorrow. Yet the Father is good and loves humanity. He listens to the soul that calls on him, and he sends it the light of salvation. Therefore, through the Spirit, he said to the prophet:

Say to the children of my people:

“[If] your sins reach [from earth to] heaven,
and if they are [red] as scarlet
and blacker than sackcloth,
[and if …][a] you return to me with your whole soul
and say to me, ‘My Father!’
I will listen to you as a holy people.”
(1 Clement 8:3)

Another passage says, “This is what the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, says: ‘If you return and weep, you will be saved. Then you will understand where you were when you placed your hope in what is empty.’” (Isaiah 30:15)

In another passage he said:

Jerusalem wept bitterly and said, “Have pity on me.” He will show you grace when he hears you weeping. When he saw, he answered you. The Lord will give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction. From now on, those who lie to you will no longer come near you. Your own eyes will see those who lie to you.
(Isaiah 30:19–20)

Therefore, we should pray to God night and day. We should stretch out our hands to him like sailors in the middle of the sea. Such people pray to God with their whole heart, sincerely and without pretending. Those who pray while pretending only lie to themselves. God examines our inner selves and searches the deepest parts of our hearts so that he may know who deserves salvation. No one who still loves the realm of lies deserves salvation.

So the poet writes:

Odysseus sat on the island in sorrow and pain.
He turned away from Calypso’s words and charms,
longing to see his village again,
with smoke rising from it.
If he had not [received] help from Heaven,
[he could not have returned] to his village. (Homer, Odyssey 1.48–1.59)

[Helen also] says:

My heart changed within me;
[words are missing] I wanted to return home. (Homer, Odyssey 4.260–261)

She mourned and said:

Aphrodite misled me
and took me away from my village.
I left behind my own daughter
and my husband, who was good, intelligent, and handsome. (Homer, Odyssey 4.261–4.264)

For when the soul leaves her perfect husband because of the unfaithfulness of Aphrodite—who comes into existence in this context through begetting—the soul comes to harm. But if she mourns and repents[a], she will be brought back home.

When Sabaoth, Yaldabaoth’s son, saw the power of that angel, he repented[a]. He sentenced his father and his mother, Matter, to judgment, and he reviled her.

He sang songs of praise to Sophia above and to her daughter Zoe. Sophia and Zoe raised him to a high position and put him in charge of the seventh heaven. After this, Sabaoth made a huge chariot of cherubim with four faces. He also made countless angels to serve him, along with harps and lyres.

Sophia brought her daughter Zoe and seated her at his right hand. There Zoe taught him about the eighth heaven. Sophia placed the angel of wrath at his left hand.

From that day on, his right hand was called “life,” while his left hand represented the injustice of the Autocrat’s upper realm. All this happened before you existed.

Look, I have now taught you about the pattern from which the rulers were formed, the matter in which that pattern was revealed, and their parent and their world.

2. When Asher was 125 years old and still healthy, he said to his children, “Children of Asher, listen to me, your father. I will show you everything that is right before God.

3. God has given humanity two ways, two purposes, two kinds of action, two modes of life, and two outcomes.

4. Everything, then, has two opposing sides, each set against the other.

5. There are two ways: good and evil. Within us are two purposes that distinguish between them.[b]

6. If a soul desires to walk in the good way, it does all its deeds in righteousness. Even if it sins, it immediately repents[c].

9. Whenever such a soul begins to do good in an evil way, it drives the deed’s outcome toward evil, because the storehouse of its purpose is filled with an evil spirit.

10. My children, obey your father, and bury me near my ancestors.”

11. Then he drew up his feet and fell asleep in peace.

12. Five years later, they carried him up to Hebron and laid him with his ancestors.

records.after_text:
Therefore, my children, be careful to obey the Lord’s commandments. Follow the truth with a single face—that is, with an undivided heart. Double-faced people receive a double punishment, because they both do evil and approve of those who do it. They imitate the spirits of deceit and contend against humanity.

So, my children, keep the law of the Lord. Do not treat evil as if it were good. Fix your attention on what is truly good. Hold to it in everything the Lord commands; live by it and find your rest in it. The way people’s lives end reveals whether they are righteous, and they become known to the angels of the Lord and of Beliar. When a wicked soul departs at death, the evil spirit torments it—the spirit it served through its lusts and wicked deeds. But if a soul is peaceful and joyful, it recognizes the angel of peace and rejoices in him. When that soul dies, he leads it into eternal life. It does not enter Beliar’s destruction, as the souls of sinners do.

You see, then, that in the last times the sons of truth will escape the spirits of deceit and Beliar, but the sons of lawlessness will be destroyed. The lawless will surrender their souls to Beliar in confusion, but the truthful will be found in joy. Every double-faced person who says, “I am for the Lord,” is really serving Beliar, and his deeds belong to the evil one.

Be convinced, my children, that everything has two ways: one good and one evil. Within us are two inclinations by which we recognize these ways. If a soul delights in good, all its deeds are righteous; and if it sins, it immediately repents[a]. Because its mind is fixed on righteousness and it hates wickedness, it throws off evil and uproots sin.

But if a soul leans toward evil, all its deeds are wicked. It rejects good, clings to evil, and is ruled by Beliar. Even when it does something good, it twists that good toward evil. It may begin by doing good, but it turns the final result toward evil, because the storehouse of its desires is filled with an evil spirit.

A person may steal, act unjustly, plunder, and defraud others, yet still show compassion to the poor. This person also has two faces, but the whole of his conduct is evil. He cheats his neighbor, provokes God, and swears falsely by the Most High, yet he has pity on the poor. He rejects and provokes the Lord who gave the law, yet he gives relief to the poor. He defiles his soul while pleasing his body. He kills many but shows mercy to a few. This person also has two faces.

Another person avoids adultery and sexual immorality and abstains from certain foods. Yet while fasting he does evil, using his power and wealth to ruin many people. However great his goodness may be, he still practices lawlessness. This person also has two faces. Such people are like hares: they appear clean, like animals with divided hooves, but in fact they are unclean. For this is what God said on the tablets of the commandments.

But do not become like Sodom, my children. It failed to recognize the angels of the Lord and was destroyed forever. I know that you will sin and be handed over to your enemies. Your land will become desolate, your holy places will be destroyed, and you will be scattered to the four corners of the earth. Among the scattered peoples you will be like water that vanishes.

This will continue until the Most High visits the earth. He himself will come as a man, eating and drinking with human beings, and he will crush the head of the dragon in the water. He will save Israel and all the nations: God will speak as a man.

Therefore tell these things to your children also, so that they may disobey him.[1] For I know that they will certainly become lawless. They will not listen to God’s law but will follow human commandments. They will be scattered like leaves driven by the wind and like water dispersed.

But you, my children, if you live in holiness according to the Lord’s commandments, you will once again dwell in safety, and all Israel will be gathered to the Lord.

1. This is a copy of the words Gad spoke to his sons when he was 125 years old:[a]

2. “My children, listen to the truth. Do what is right and obey the whole law of the Most High. Do not follow the spirit of hatred, because it makes every human deed evil.

3. A person does not want to see or hear anyone he hates. He hates anyone who speaks about the Lord, treating him as though he were an accuser. He envies anyone who prospers and resents anyone who is rich. He refuses to praise the brave. He slanders the truthful, begrudges the successful, and loves the arrogant and lawless. Hatred blinds his soul. I learned this from what happened between Joseph and me.

4. I began to hate Joseph when he told our father that the sons of Zilpah and Bilhah were slaughtering the best animals from the flock and eating them without Judah and Joseph.

5. Joseph told our father that I had said, ‘I saw a bear mauling a lamb. I chased the bear and killed it, but the lamb could not survive, so I slaughtered it, and we ate it.’

6. Because of this, I remained angry with Joseph until the day he was sold.

7. The spirit of hatred was in me. I did not want to hear Joseph with my ears or see him with my eyes, because he rebuked us openly. He said that we were eating animals from the flock without Judah.

8. Our father believed everything Joseph told him.

9. My children, I now confess my sin: I hated Joseph from my heart and often wanted to kill him.

10. I hated him even more because of his dreams. I wanted to wipe him from the earth as an ox devours grass in a field.

11. So Judah and I sold him to the Ishmaelites for thirty pieces of gold.[b]

12. But the Lord of our fathers did not let us act so wickedly toward him that we killed him.

13. Now, my children, I tell you: each of you must love your brother and remove hatred from your heart. Love one another by what you do, what you say, and what you truly desire.

14. When I was with my father, I spoke peacefully to Joseph. But after I left, the spirit of hatred darkened my mind and stirred me up to kill him.

15. Love one another sincerely. If someone sins against you, speak to him peacefully and do not hide deceit in your heart. If he admits his sin and repents[e], forgive him.

16. If he denies it, do not become furious with him. Otherwise, you may take his poison into yourself, swear an oath, and add your own sin to his.

17. When someone is quarreling with you, do not trust him with your secrets. He may come to hate you, become your enemy, and commit some serious sin against you. People often speak craftily or pretend to be friendly because they intend harm.

18. If he denies his wrongdoing because your correction has made him ashamed, say no more. His denial shows his shame and repentance, and he will stop wronging you. He will honor and respect you and live at peace with you.

19. But if he has no shame and continues doing wrong, still forgive him from your heart and leave vengeance to God.

20. If someone becomes rich through injustice, do not envy him. Wait for the end the Lord has appointed.

21. Even if he gives back twice what he took, do not be troubled. Wait patiently until the Lord brings judgment.

22. A poor person who is free from envy pleases the Lord in everything and is blessed beyond all others, because he is spared the burden of those who chase empty things.

23. Therefore, remove envy from your souls and love one another with sincere and upright hearts.

24. Teach these things to your children too, so that they may honor Levi and Judah. From these two the Lord will raise up salvation for Israel.

25. I know that in the last days you will turn away from the Lord. You will live lawlessly, mistreat Levi, and fight against Judah.

26. But you will not defeat them, because an angel of the Lord guides them both. Through them Israel will remain standing.

27. When you turn away from the Lord, you will do every kind of evil and commit the detestable acts of the nations. You will be led astray by women who practice lawlessness, while wicked spirits fill you with every kind of malice.

28. I have read in the book of righteous Enoch that your prince is Satan. It says that all the spirits of sexual immorality and arrogance will follow the sons of Levi and cause them to sin against the Lord.[c]

29. My sons will join the sons of Levi and share in all their sins. The sons of Judah will become greedy and seize other people’s possessions like lions.

30. Therefore, you will be taken away with them as captives. There you will suffer all the plagues of Egypt and all the evils of the nations.

31. So when you return to the Lord, live with integrity and do what is right in everything. Treat each neighbor with mercy and truth.

32. If you return to the Lord with sincere hearts, put away hatred and lawlessness, and love one another from the heart, then you will have peace.

33. No human being will be able to defeat you, because the God of heaven will be among you and will bring peace to you and to all Israel.

34. No enemy will celebrate your defeat, and every wild animal will fear you. The Lord will bless everything you do and say.

35. Now, my children, fear the Lord God of heaven, and guard yourselves against Satan and his spirits.

36. Draw near to God and to the angel who intercedes for you. This angel is a mediator between God and humanity for the peace of Israel.[d]

37. He will oppose the enemy’s kingdom. That is why the enemy is eager to destroy everyone who calls on the Lord.

38. The enemy knows that his kingdom will end on the day Israel repents.

39. The angel of peace himself will strengthen Israel and keep it from falling into the worst evil.

40. Even when Israel is living lawlessly, the Lord will not abandon them. He will transform them into a nation that does his will, for no angel is equal to the Lord.

41. His name will be known everywhere in Israel and among the nations.

42. Therefore, my children, keep yourselves from every lawless act. Remove all hatred and falsehood from your lives, and love truth and patience.

43. Pass on to your children everything you heard from your father, so that the Savior of the nations may receive you. He is true and patient, gentle and humble, and by his deeds he teaches God’s law.[d]

44. Turn away from all wrongdoing and hold firmly to God’s righteousness. Then your descendants will be saved forever.

45. After Gad gave them these commands, he told them to bury him in Hebron.

46. Then, after a long life, he fell into the peaceful sleep of death.

47. His sons did as he had commanded. They carried him to Hebron and buried him with his ancestors.”

Tell your children these things too:

They must honor Levi and Judah, because from them the Lord will raise up salvation for Israel.[a] Tell them also to love Joseph. He remained innocent through every hardship and obeyed God’s command instead of returning evil for evil. Although his brothers made him suffer greatly and plotted against him, he loved them and spoke peaceably to them.

Now, my children, I command you to love one another sincerely. If someone sins against you, speak peaceably to him without hiding deceit in your heart. If he admits his sin and repents[d], forgive him. But if he denies it, do not let the dispute become heated. Otherwise, he may take in the quarrel’s poison, begin to swear, and add a second sin to the first.[b]

If someone prospers more than you do, do not resent it. Instead, pray that he may receive every good thing in full. If someone is honored, do not envy him; if someone becomes rich, do not be jealous. Bless the Lord, who gives good things to everyone. A poor person who is free from envy is rich in the Lord’s sight.

Do not hate a beautiful woman because of her appearance, or a man because he receives great honor. God gives the good things of the earth to whomever he chooses.

Act with integrity, and pray for your neighbor so that you will not become jealous when things go well for him. A jealous person is always troubled, and a hateful person is always darkened within. Love one another in what you do, what you say, and what you intend in your heart. I myself spoke peaceably to Joseph while secretly intending to kill him.

The spirit of hatred is evil. It is never at peace with anyone but always desires their downfall. It weakens the body, disturbs the soul, and fills the mind with anger.

Therefore, when someone does evil to you, do good to him and pray for him. Then the Lord will redeem you from every evil. If a shameless or lawless person prospers, do not be jealous. Wait to see what outcome the Lord brings.[c] He may receive his reward in this life, or he may be kept for punishment and repaid at the judgment.

A poor person who is free from envy is blessed above everyone else, even without wealth, because he possesses treasure that cannot perish. So cast away hatred and love one another with upright hearts.

1. While I was there, Barshaba king of Adullam welcomed us generously and held a feast with plenty of wine. At his urging, I took his daughter Shua as my wife.

2. She bore me Er, Onan, and Shelah. The Lord killed the first two. Er was wicked. Onan married Tamar, but at his mother’s command he spilled his seed on the ground. He too died because of his wickedness.

3. Shelah lived, but I did not give Tamar to him as his wife. I thought, “He might also die like his brothers.” I did not know that the Lord was judging me for what I had done at Timnah to my father Jacob and to Joseph.

4. Tamar remained a widow. Two years later, I heard that she was going up to Timnah for the sheep shearing, and I also went there to shear my sheep.

5. When she learned that I was going, she dressed like a bride and sat by the gate of the city of Enaim. According to an Amorite custom, a woman who was about to marry would sit by the gate for seven days and offer herself for sex.[a]

6. I was drunk with wine and did not recognize her. Her beauty and the way she had adorned herself led my mind astray.

7. I turned aside to her and said, “Let me sleep with you.”

She asked, “What will you give me if I let you sleep with me?”

8. I answered, “I will send you a young goat from my flock.”

She asked, “Will you give me something as a pledge until you send it?”

9. I said, “What pledge should I give you?”

She answered, “Your staff, your belt, and your royal diadem.”[b]

10. I gave them to her and slept with her, and she conceived a child by me. Because of the wine, I did not understand what I had done. I still did not recognize her when I left.

11. Later I sent the young goat, but my servant could not find her. I asked the local people, “Where is the woman who sat beside the road at Enaim?”

12. They answered, “No prostitute has been here, and no stranger has sat by the gate.” Then I understood that I had sinned. But I kept the matter secret because I was ashamed.

13. Three months later, someone told me, “Tamar, your daughter-in-law, has acted as a prostitute, and now she is pregnant.” In my foolish and arrogant anger I said, “Bring her out and burn her!”

14. As they were bringing her out, she secretly sent me the staff, belt, and diadem. She said, “I am pregnant by the man who owns these.”

15. I recognized them and was ashamed. I said, “Tamar is more righteous than I am, because I did not give her to my son Shelah.” I never slept with her again.

16. So now, my children, I tell you: do not get drunk with wine. Wine turns the mind away from truth, stirs up lust, and causes the eyes to mislead you.

17. The spirit of sexual immorality uses wine as its servant to give the mind pleasure. Together they rob a person of understanding.

18. When someone drinks until he is drunk, wine fills his mind with filthy thoughts and drives his body toward sex. If he then has an opportunity to satisfy his desire, he sins without shame.

19. This is what a drunkard is like, my children. A drunk person respects no one. Wine caused me to break God’s commandment and sleep with Tamar. I felt no shame before the crowds in the city, but publicly brought shame on my sons by sleeping with her.

20. After drinking wine, I disregarded God’s commandment and took a Canaanite woman as my wife.[c] Therefore, my children, anyone who drinks wine needs great self-control.

21. This is the self-control needed when drinking wine: a person may drink if he remains modest and does not fall into shameless conduct.

22. But if he goes beyond the limit, the spirit of deceit attacks his mind. It makes the drunkard speak obscenely and sin without shame. He may even boast about his disgrace as if it were something glorious.

23. A person who commits sexual immorality does not realize what he is losing and feels no shame when he is dishonored. Even a king who commits sexual immorality loses his kingship by becoming its servant. This is what happened to me.

24. I gave away my staff, which represented the support of my tribe; my belt, which represented my power; and my diadem, which represented the glory of my kingdom.

25. I truly repented[f] of these things. I ate no meat and drank no wine until my old age, and I experienced no joy.

26. God’s angel showed me that women rule over kings and beggars alike. They take glory from a king, strength from a strong man, and even the little support that a beggar has in his poverty.

27. Therefore, my children, guard yourselves against sexual immorality and the love of money. Listen to your father Judah.

28. These things draw people away from God’s law and blind the desires of the soul. They teach arrogance and keep people from showing compassion to their neighbors.

29. They strip the soul of everything good, burden a person with hard labor and trouble, drive away sleep, and consume the body.

30. They keep a person from offering sacrifices to God and from remembering to bless him. When such a person hears a prophet speak, he takes offense and becomes angry.

31. He is enslaved to two opposing passions and cannot obey God. They have blinded his soul, so even in daylight he walks as though it were night.

32. My children, I have shown you that wine leads to sexual immorality and that the love of money leads to idolatry. Both turn the mind away from God’s law.

33. Therefore, live soberly in truth and in reverence for God. Otherwise, you will perish through every kind of evil deed and affliction—especially if gifts lead you astray, and you marry Canaanite women and bind yourselves to their wealth.

34. I know that after my death your descendants will act lawlessly and fight against Levi. They will not defeat him, because the angel of the Lord guides him, while the spirit of deceit has misled me.

35. Now I command you to love Levi so that you may live. Do not exalt yourselves against him, or you will be utterly destroyed.

36. The Lord gave me the kingship and gave Levi the priesthood. He placed the kingship under the priesthood.

37. He gave me authority over earthly things, but gave Levi authority over heavenly things.

38. Just as heaven is higher than earth, so God’s priesthood is higher than earthly kingship—unless the priesthood turns away from the Lord through sin and comes under the rule of an earthly kingdom.[d]

39. The angel of the Lord told me, “The Lord chose Levi before you to be near him, and he chose you to reign with Levi like a lion.”

40. Therefore, do not exalt yourselves over Levi or oppose me. Fully honor the Lord in both offices, and among the people remain close to Levi.

41. Because of Levi, the Lord will choose the kingship from among your descendants and the priesthood from among Levi’s. In this way the Lord will be present for all the nations and for the people of Israel.

42. I have now given you these commands because I read in the books of righteous Enoch that your descendants will turn away from the Lord and commit every kind of wickedness and cause every kind of suffering before him.[e]

2 Two years after the death of his brother Joseph, Reuben became sick. Joseph’s sons and grandsons gathered to visit him. 3 Reuben said to them, “My children, I am dying. I am going where my ancestors have gone.”

Now, my children, listen to me about what I saw during my repentance[d]: the seven spirits of deceit.[a] Then seven spirits were given to oppose humanity. They are the chief sources of the sins of youth.[b]

Seven other spirits were given to humanity at creation, so that every human activity would have its place within them. The first is the spirit of life, which forms a person’s whole makeup. The second is the spirit of sight, which gives rise to desire. The third is the spirit of hearing, through which we receive instruction. The fourth is the spirit of smell, which produces sensations of taste for drawing in air and breathing.[c] The fifth is the spirit of speech, through which knowledge comes. The sixth is the spirit of taste, through which we eat food and drink. It builds strength, because food is the basis of strength. The seventh is the spirit of procreation and sexual intercourse. Through it, sins come together because of the love of pleasure.

Therefore, this spirit is last in creation and first in youth, because it is full of ignorance. It leads a young man into a pit as though he were blind, and over a cliff like an animal.

1. Therefore, my children, do not focus on the beauty of women or fill your minds with what they do. Instead, live with sincere, undivided hearts and in fear of the Lord. Work hard at doing good, learning, and caring for your flocks until the Lord gives you the wife he chooses for you, so that you may not suffer as I did.

2. Until my father died, I did not have the courage to look him in the face.[a]

3. The disgrace of my sin continually ate away at my mind.

4. For seven months I was so sick that I nearly died. Then I repented[e] before the Lord with firm resolve, and the spirit of jealousy left me.[b] Ever since then, I have remained on guard and have not sinned.

5. Therefore, my children, I tell you: obey everything I command you, and you will certainly not sin.

6. Sexual immorality is a pit for the soul. It separates the soul from God and draws it near to idols. It leads both mind and understanding astray and brings young men down to Hades before their time.

7. Sexual immorality has destroyed many people. Whether a man is old or noble, rich or poor, he brings disgrace on himself before others and becomes a stumbling block to Beliar.[c]

8. You have heard how Joseph guarded himself from a woman. He cleansed his thoughts of every kind of sexual immorality and found favor with God and people.

9. The Egyptian woman tried many things against him. She called in magicians and brought him potions.[d] But Joseph guarded himself from every evil desire and refused to consent inwardly to wicked lust.

10. Therefore, the God of your fathers rescued him from every hidden evil and from death.

After Joseph had been thrown into the pit,[a] my brothers sat down to eat and drink. But I felt deep compassion for Joseph and did not eat. I stayed near the pit to guard him because Judah feared that Simeon and Gad[b] might suddenly attack and kill him. When my brothers saw that I was not eating, they appointed me to guard Joseph until he was sold. He remained in the pit for three days and three nights and was sold without having eaten.

When Reuben returned and learned that Joseph had been sold while he was away, he tore his clothes in mourning. He cried, “How can I face my father Jacob?” He took the silver and ran after the merchants, but he could not find them. They had left the main road and taken a shorter route through the land of the Troglodytes.[c] Reuben was overcome with grief and ate no food that day.

Then Dan came to him and said, “Do not weep or be distressed. We have decided what to tell our father. Let us use a sword to slaughter a male goat and stain Joseph’s tunic with its blood. Then we will send it to our father Jacob and say, ‘See whether this is your son’s tunic.’” They did this, and Jacob mourned for Joseph for the rest of his life.[d]

My brothers became afraid, and they all repented[g] of what they had done to Joseph. But the Egyptians and Ishmaelites did not harm him, because the Lord did not allow them to do evil to him.

Joseph was handsome and pleasing in appearance. He had no spite in him but was gentle, sincere, and free from deceit. Therefore, my children, show compassion, because compassion is good for everyone. Even if someone is a sinner, the Lord will count his compassion as righteousness. But even if someone prospers, the Lord will destroy him if he has no compassion.

During the famine, I remembered the Lord’s compassion and gave food to every stranger, orphan, and widow. I did not marry until I was forty years old, because I had spent my life in hard work and had gained no wealth in my simplicity. My father had blessed me, saying, “Your sons will be like a safe haven for sailors and a harbor for ships.”

Now, my children, I command you to treat everyone with mercy and compassion, so that the Lord may also have compassion on you. In the last days you will turn away from the Lord. You will make Levi angry and rise against Judah, but you will not defeat them. An angel of the Lord will guide them both, because through them Israel will stand.

Whenever you turn away from the Lord, you will follow every kind of evil and practice the detestable acts of the nations. You will go astray after women and become enslaved to every wickedness as spirits of deceit work within you. I have read in the writing of Enoch that in the last days your descendants will also become corrupt. They will break the law against Levi’s descendants and sin against Judah, but they will not be able to stand against them. From Levi the Lord will raise up a priest, and from Judah a king, God and man.[e] He will save all the nations and the people of Israel.

Now I command you, my children: obey me, your father Zebulun. Show mercy to your neighbors and compassion to everyone—not only to people but also to livestock. Because I did this, the Lord blessed me. When all my brothers became sick, I remained healthy, for the Lord knows each person’s intentions.

Therefore, my children, let compassion come from deep within you. The Lord will treat people as they treat their neighbors. I saw my brothers’ sons become sick and die because they had no compassion, but my sons were kept safe, as you know. In the land of Canaan, I never profited by using dishonest scales or two different measures in trade. Instead, I shared everything I owned with everyone, with a sincere and undivided heart. I held no evil against anyone, and I kept my integrity in everything even into old age.

You too, my children, must keep the law of the Lord. Show mercy to your neighbors and compassion to everyone—not only to people but also to animals. Because I did this, I received mercy from the Lord, everyone blessed me, and the Lord increased my possessions a thousandfold. A compassionate person does good to his own soul.

Know this, my children: in the last times you will turn away from the Lord. You will be divided within Israel, follow two evils, and have no place in the assembly of the righteous. But after this, the Lord himself will arise for you as the light of righteousness. He will heal and save everyone. He will bring back those held captive by Beliar,[f] turn disobedient hearts back to the Lord, and give everlasting peace to those who call on him.

The holy ones will rest in Eden, and the righteous will rejoice in the New Jerusalem, which will display God’s glory forever. Jerusalem will no longer be left desolate, and Israel will no longer be taken captive. The Lord will be in Jerusalem, living among humanity. The Holy One of Israel will reign over them in humility and poverty, and whoever believes in him will reign in truth in heaven.

Now, my children, fear the Lord your God, and guard yourselves against Satan and his spirits. Draw near to God and to the angel who intercedes for you. This angel is a mediator between God and humanity for the peace of Israel. He will oppose the enemy’s kingdom, so the enemy is eager to destroy everyone who calls on the Lord. The enemy knows that his kingdom will end on the day Israel repents.

The angel of peace himself will strengthen Israel so that it does not fall into the lowest depths of evil. When Israel breaks the law, the Lord will not abandon his people. He will transform them into a nation that does his will. No angel is equal to him, and his name is known everywhere in Israel and among the nations.

Therefore, keep yourselves from every evil deed. Cast away hatred and every kind of deceit. Love one another sincerely and patiently. Pass on to your children what I heard from my father, so that the Savior of the nations may receive you. He is gentle and humble, and by his own example he teaches God’s law.

Flee from all unrighteousness and hold firmly to the righteousness taught in the Lord’s law. Then your descendants will continue forever, and every generation of your family will be blessed.

After Zebulun had given them these commands, he stretched out his feet and died at a good old age. His sons placed him in a coffin. Later they carried him to Hebron and buried him with his ancestors.

records.after_text:
However, he was a <helper> who rescued them from their mistaken thinking and rebellion. From him came the conversion called “repentance[b].” This happened when the Word changed his opinion and his way of thinking. He turned away from evil and toward what is good.

After this conversion, he remembered those who exist. He also remembered the prayer for the one who had turned himself through what is good. First he prayed to the one who lives in the Fullness,[a] and he remembered him. Then he remembered his brothers—each one separately and all of them together. But before them all, he remembered the Father.

Their united prayer helped him return to himself and to the Totality. He remembered those who had existed from the beginning because he himself had been remembered. This remembrance was like a distant thought calling from far away and bringing him back.

His whole prayer and remembrance consisted of several powers. They agreed with the limit mentioned earlier, because nothing in his thought is barren. These powers were good and greater than the powers of the likeness, which also belong to a [dark] nature. What they became came from an illusion involving similarity and from a [vain thought] of pride. They also came from [a thought] that knew them first.

What were those former beings like? They were like <oblivion> and deep sleep. They resembled people having disturbing dreams, pursued and troubled by <someone> while they slept. But to him, the others were like beings filled with light waiting for sunrise, because they saw sweet dreams in him.

At once, the things produced by the thought <ceased>. They no longer had substance or honor, because they were not equal to those who had existed before them. If they stood above the likenesses, it was only because they acted with good intentions. They had not arisen from the weakness that had come into being. Their good intention belonged to <the one who> sought the glorious one who existed before all things, after praying and raising himself toward the good.

He planted in them a desire to seek and pray to the glorious one who existed before them. He also gave them the ability to think of [him], and the ability to think that something greater than themselves had existed before they did, even though they did not know what it was. This thought produced harmony and mutual love among them, so they acted with unity and a shared purpose. After all, unity and shared purpose were the source of their existence.

source_evidence.exact_excerpt: זִֽבְחֵ֣י אֱלֹהִים֮ ר֪וּחַ נִשְׁבָּ֫רָ֥ה לֵב נִשְׁבָּ֥ר וְ/נִדְכֶּ֑ה אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לֹ֣א תִבְזֶֽה־׃
source_evidence.limitation: Contextual editorial review of recorded evidence, not independent scholarly or manuscript certification.
